subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: Should `gh-issues` hardening require a runtime/content-boundary change for issue and review text, or is prompt-level guidance plus the separate child tool-allowlist work sufficient for OpenClaw's supported trust model?
rationale: The source evidence proves the current data path remains, but the durable fix crosses security posture, task-prompt structure, and delegated tool-policy semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary alone.

options.title: Require runtime content boundary
options.body: Keep this issue open until `gh-issues` issue and review content is wrapped, summarized, or otherwise passed as untrusted data, with sandbox or child tool policy applied where needed.

options.title: Accept prompt guidance only
options.body: Treat the open bundled-skill prompt guard as enough defense in depth and explicitly accept the residual template-injection risk under the current trust model.

options.title: Split the work
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/15032 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78441 own child capability scoping while keeping a separate, narrower tracker for the `gh-issues` content boundary.

recommendation.title: Require runtime content boundary
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until `gh-issues` issue and review content is wrapped, summarized, or otherwise passed as untrusted data, with sandbox or child tool policy applied where needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and adjacent source ownership point to the subagent runtime and task prompt boundary where the security decision lands.
